title: Favourites for signed-in customers

sourcesRead.contributes: auth (Bearer token from POST /users/login), OpenAPI excerpt: GET/POST /favorites, DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId}, statuses 200/201/204/401/409, request field product_id

actors: signed-in customer (web shop and mobile app through the API)
context: Signed-in customers keep a personal list of favourite products, from the product page of the web shop and through the shop API used by the mobile app.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: A signed-in customer adds a product to favourites with POST /favorites; the API responds 201 with the favourite (its id and the product id).
acceptanceCriteria.text: A signed-in customer adds a product to favourites with POST /favorites; the API responds 201 with the favourite (its id and the product id).
outcomes: the response body is the favourite and contains its id
the response body contains the product id that was added

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Adding a product that is already a favourite is rejected and the list still contains it once.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Adding a product that is already a favourite is rejected and the list still contains it once.
outcomes: adding the same product again → 409 (the product is already a favourite)
GET /favorites afterwards contains that product exactly once

acceptanceCriteria.quote: GET /favorites lists the customer's own favourites only; another customer's favourites are never included.
acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /favorites lists the customer's own favourites only; another customer's favourites are never included.
outcomes: the list contains the customer's own favourites
no favourite of another customer is included

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Every favourites endpoint responds 401 without a valid token.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Every favourites endpoint responds 401 without a valid token.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: On the web shop, a signed-in customer who clicks "Add to favourites" on a product page sees "Product added to your favorites list." and the product then appears on the "Favorites" page of their account.
acceptanceCriteria.text: On the web shop, a signed-in customer who clicks "Add to favourites" on a product page sees "Product added to your favorites list." and the product then appears on the "Favorites" page of their account.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: a product page of the web shop
outcomes: after clicking "Add to favourites" the message "Product added to your favorites list." is shown
the product then appears on the "Favorites" page of the customer's account

acceptanceCriteria.quote: DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId} removes the favourite (204) and it no longer appears in GET /favorites.
acceptanceCriteria.text: DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId} removes the favourite (204) and it no longer appears in GET /favorites.
outcomes: the removed favourite no longer appears in GET /favorites

endpoints.success: 201 the favourite, with its id and the product id
endpoints.request: JSON body { product_id: string } (product_id required); header Authorization: Bearer <token>
returns the token used as Authorization: Bearer <token> (made by the profile's accounts recipe)

rules.text: Favourites are a personal list per signed-in customer: GET /favorites returns the customer's own favourites only.
A product can be a favourite only once per customer; adding it again is a conflict (409).
POST /favorites requires product_id (string) in its JSON body.

errorModel.case: Any favourites endpoint (GET /favorites, POST /favorites, DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId}) called without a valid token (no body stated)
POST /favorites for a product that is already a favourite (a conflict; no body stated)

auth.mechanism: Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer <token> on every favourites call
auth.credentials: the token from POST /users/login (the profile's accounts recipe signs each test's customer in)

testData.strategy: not stated in the sources: each test uses its own signed-in customer (seed.account()); favourites the criteria act on are created by the tests through POST /favorites

gaps.element: how a test finds the id of an existing product to put in product_id (no products endpoint or product is named)

tried.result: L23-L28 name no product and no way to list products
the OpenAPI excerpt covers favourites only (L7); product_id is a string (L28), no source for it

Existing catalogue products from GET /products (page 1, data[].id, ULID strings); POST /favorites accepted such an id as product_id (201). Action pickCatalogueProducts; same GET /products as readWholeCatalogue, proven by TOOL-1

gaps.value: Existing catalogue products from GET /products (page 1, data[].id, ULID strings); POST /favorites accepted such an id as product_id (201). Action pickCatalogueProducts; same GET /products as readWholeCatalogue, proven by TOOL-1

gaps.element: web shop product page: its route and how the "Add to favourites" button and the confirmation message are found

tried.result: L27 names the button label and message but no route or locator

Route /product/{productId}; the product's name is heading data-test=product-name; the button is getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to favourites', exact: true }) (data-test=add-to-favorites, 1 match); the confirmation is shown as the page's role=alert with the text (getByText matches 1); the click calls POST /favorites (201)

gaps.value: Route /product/{productId}; the product's name is heading data-test=product-name; the button is getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to favourites', exact: true }) (data-test=add-to-favorites, 1 match); the confirmation is shown as the page's role=alert with the text (getByText matches 1); the click calls POST /favorites (201)

gaps.element: the "Favorites" page of the customer's account: its route and how the listed products are found

tried.result: L27 names the page "Favorites" of the account, no route or locator

Route /account/favorites (account menu 'My favorites'), loads GET /favorites; each favourite is a card data-test=favorite-<favourite id> whose product name is data-test=product-name: locator('[data-test^="favorite-"]').getByTestId('product-name')

gaps.value: Route /account/favorites (account menu 'My favorites'), loads GET /favorites; each favourite is a card data-test=favorite-<favourite id> whose product name is data-test=product-name: locator('[data-test^="favorite-"]').getByTestId('product-name')
